mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If high FEDFUNDS does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE above 5% does not lead to negative returns in 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth without corresponding employment growth indicates inefficient expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth with lagging employment does not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production in late-cycle expansion signals supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production slowdown does not lead to negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 3% may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI above 3% does not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: High FEDFUNDS coupled with rising UNRATE indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If high FEDFUNDS and rising UNRATE do not lead to negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1300 indicate weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If low housing starts do not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: Decline in real consumer spending signals weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decline does not lead to negative returns.
